parsed.explanation: Police explicitly target trans women under an applied same-sex law, with arbitrary detention, imprisonment up to 3 years, routine intimidation, extortion/coerced informing, forced examinations described as torture, and impunity. No anti-discrimination protection, no registered LGBT organisations, and official hostility leave no working recourse. No execution or custody death is documented, placing this above the 0.05 tier, but organised state targeting and torture place it well below 0.25.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Arbitrary detention and prosecution of trans women under Article 120; forced examinations amounting to torture; police ill-treatment and impunity persisting.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Discovery can trigger detention, forced examination, imprisonment up to 3 years, and extortion or coerced informing, with no documented remedy.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Article 120 applied in cases 2009-2023; police routinely target gay/bi men and trans women, intimidate, exploit, extort and coerce informing; official hostility documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: The criminal statute functions as an active police lever against trans women, not a dormant law, amplified by official hostility and societal harassment.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police violence, blackmail, extortion and discrimination by state and non-state actors; continuing societal harassment and rural-taboo discrimination.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police are documented perpetrators rather than protectors, with impunity for ill-treatment and almost no legal protection for victims.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination protection; sexual orientation omitted from 2023 constitution; LGBT organisations cannot register and operate unofficially; impunity persists.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of lawful organisations, constitutional protection and effective accountability leaves detention, extortion and torture without working recourse.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: document/presentation cases lead to interrogation abuse, beatings/extortion and years in prison with dismissed complaints. This dossier lacks documented custody deaths or capital charging, so slightly higher than 0.15, but torture and imprisonment are both documented.

Lower: 0.25-B has extortion and short detention without torture or a proved imprisonment regime. Here forced examinations are described as torture, arbitrary detention and prosecution are patterned, and impunity is documented, indicating a more severe state hand.

Well below: 0.35-B involves stops, confiscation and fines with detention rarely becoming imprisonment. Here prosecution, imprisonment, routine police violence and torture are documented, so consequences after outing are materially worse.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is nationally uniform: an applied criminal provision gives police a lever used systematically against trans women for detention, forced examinations described as torture, bribes and coerced informing, while official hostility, societal harassment, no anti-discrimination law and unregistered organisations remove recourse. Entry, facilities and care are undocumented and cannot be credited as safety; the documented enforcement interaction drives the rating. No execution is documented, distinguishing this from the 0.05 tier.
